target: Bract (PO:0009055) absent only at the outside of the fig opening (syconium ostiole FLOPO:0986063), with context 'external ostiolar'. The hyaline bracts that are described are other bracts (interfloral or internal ostiolar bracts), so they stay present and transparent (PATO:0000964)
fix: In Ficus, 'ostiole without external bracts' or 'ostiole sans bractées externes' denies only the external ostiolar bracts. Keep 'external ostiolar' as the context, with syconium ostiole FLOPO:0986063 as the place. Never record a taxon-wide 'bract absent'.
reason: Ficus figs always have ostiolar bracts. The text only says that none show on the outside.

target: Culm (stem PO:0009047) aphyllopodic (FLOPO:0991233): the lower or basal sheaths have no blade. The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) of the true leaves is present and flat
fix: In Cyperaceae and Poaceae, 'sans limbe', 'bladeless' and 'without blade' describe particular sheaths (basal, lower or bract sheaths). Read them as culm + aphyllopodic FLOPO:0991233, or as leaf sheath PO:0020104 with the position as context. Never read them as a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: The blades are described as flat, so only some sheaths lack a blade.

target: Lenticel (PO:0000031) absent on the young branches (branch PO:0025073, context 'rameaux' or young branchlets). The large lenticels are on another member, most likely older stems or the fruit (PO:0009001). Keep the member named in each sentence as the context
fix: 'rameaux non lenticellés' and 'branchlets not lenticellate' restrict the absence to the branches. Keep 'branch' as the bearer and context. Never record a taxon-wide 'lenticel absent' when lenticels on another organ (fruit, trunk, older stems) are described.
reason: In Strychnos, the young twigs often lack lenticels while the fruits or old stems have large ones. The record does not show which member the second sentence is about.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) absent only on the side of the fig body, with context 'lateral' (on the receptacle). The basal bracts are present and subverticillate (whorled), with context 'basal'
fix: In Ficus, 'without lateral bracts' denies only the bracts on the side of the fig body. Keep 'lateral' as the context and the basal bracts as a separate statement. Never record a taxon-wide 'bract absent'.
reason: Ficus figs have basal bracts and may or may not have lateral ones. The two statements are about different bracts.

target: Cystoliths absent. PO and FLOPO have no cystolith class, so make no part-and-quality statement for now (record it later as 'cystoliths absent in the leaf lamina'). The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) is present and chartaceous
fix: 'cystoliths absent', 'cystoliths present' and 'without cystoliths' are about cell inclusions, not the organ that holds them. Never move the absence onto the leaf or lamina. Drop the statement until a cystolith class exists.
reason: The lamina is described as chartaceous, so it exists. Only the cystoliths in it are missing.

target: Trichome (PO:0000282) absent, with context 'internal' (the inside wall of the fig, i.e. among the flowers). The fig (fruit PO:0009001) is present, with the apex convex
fix: 'internal hairs absent', 'interfloral hairs absent' and 'without internal hairs' map to trichome PO:0000282 absent, with 'internal' as the context. The absence never falls back to the fig or fruit that holds the hairs.
reason: The fig is described, so it exists. Only the hairs inside it are missing.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) absent, with context 'lateral' (on the fig body). The fig (fruit PO:0009001) is present and subglobose
fix: 'without lateral bracts' maps to bract PO:0009055 absent, with context 'lateral'. It never maps to the fig, receptacle or fruit that carries the bracts.
reason: The fig is described as subglobose. The absence names bracts, not the fig.

target: No absence statement. The bracts (PO:0009055) are present but fall early: deciduous (generic), as recorded
fix: '<part> not seen, caducous' and 'bracts not seen' mean the part falls early and was not on the specimens. Keep the caducous quality and never record an absence.
reason: 'Not seen' reports missing material, and 'caducous' explains why.

target: The lower surface of the leaf lamina (PO:0020039) is not dotted: punctate (PATO:0001512), negated. Nothing is absent. Also, 'grey-glaucous' was read as 'green', which is a wrong quality on the other statement
fix: In Myristicaceae, 'dots absent', 'without dots' and 'dots and dashes absent' describe a feature of the lower leaf surface, not the leaf. Read them as lamina not punctate (PATO:0001512) or drop them. Never record 'leaf lamina absent'. 'Glaucous' and 'grey-glaucous' are never 'green'.
reason: The lamina is described, so only the small dots on its lower surface are missing.

target: The lower surface of the leaf (PO:0025034) is not dotted: punctate (PATO:0001512), negated. The leaf is present and chartaceous to coriaceous
fix: Same rule as for Knema above: 'dots absent' is the leaf surface lacking dots, never 'leaf absent'.
reason: The leaves are described as chartaceous or coriaceous.

target: Gland (portion of secretory tissue PO:0005656) absent on the bract, with the bract as context. The bract (PO:0009055) is present and rather thick
fix: 'glands absent', 'eglandular' and 'without glands' map to gland PO:0005656 absent (or the organ is not glandular), with the organ as context. The absence never falls on the organ that would carry the glands.
reason: The probract is described as thick. Only its glands are missing.

target: The flowering stalk (scape, stem PO:0009047) has no leaves: cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent, with context 'flowering stalk' or 'scape'. The basal leaves (leaf PO:0025034) are present and palmately lobed
fix: In rosette plants, 'flowering stalk without leaves', 'scape leafless' and 'without leaves' said of a stalk mean cauline leaves absent on the stalk. Keep the stalk as the context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: Heuchera has basal leaves and a leafless flowering stalk.

target: Pistillode (PO:0009078) absent, with context 'male flowers' (staminate flower PO:0025600). The ovary (PO:0009072) of the female flowers is present and glabrous
fix: 'rudimentary ovary', 'ovary rudiment', 'vestigial ovary' and 'pistillode' map to pistillode PO:0009078. That is the male-flower structure, never the plant ovary. Keep the sex as the context.
reason: Diospyros has separate male and female flowers. The male flowers lack a rudimentary ovary, and the female flowers have a real one.

target: Ray flower (PO:0025331) absent. The disc florets are present and yellow, with 'disc' as the context on flower PO:0009046
fix: 'ray florets absent' maps to ray flower PO:0025331 absent, never to flower. 'disc florets <quality>' goes on flower, with context 'disc'.
reason: Emilia flower heads have only disc florets. The flowers exist and only the ray type is missing.

target: The fruit (PO:0009001) has no apical peg or beak at its apex. PO and FLOPO have no peg term, so make no part-and-quality statement, or record fruit apex not beaked. The fruit is present and elliptic
fix: 'apical peg absent', 'beak absent' and 'without a stipe or peg' describe a missing outgrowth of the fruit, never the fruit. Do not map 'peg' to gynophore (PO:0006330) in Terminalia fruit descriptions.
reason: The fruit is described as elliptic. Only the small point at its tip is missing.

target: The leaves (PO:0025034) are present but few and reduced: decreased amount (PATO:0001997) and decreased size (PATO:0000587). They are closely appressed. Nothing is absent
fix: 'nearly leafless', 'almost leafless', 'subaphyllous' and 'leafless or nearly so' qualify how many leaves there are. They are never an absence.
reason: Thesium has few, small, appressed leaves, which the second statement describes.

target: Domatium (FLOPO:0986021) absent. The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) is present and leathery
fix: 'domatia absent' and 'without domatia' map to domatium FLOPO:0986021 absent. They never fall back to the leaf or lamina that would bear the domatia.
reason: The lamina is described. Only the vein-axil domatia are missing.

target: Culm (stem PO:0009047) aphyllopodic (FLOPO:0991233): the lower sheaths have no blade. The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) of the true leaves is present and deep green
fix: In Carex, 'the lower bladeless' and 'lower sheaths bladeless' qualify the basal sheaths. Read them as culm + aphyllopodic FLOPO:0991233. Never read them as a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: The blades are described as deep green. Only the lowest sheaths have no blade.

target: Culm (stem PO:0009047) aphyllopodic (FLOPO:0991233): the lowest leaves are reduced to bladeless sheaths. The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) of the other leaves is present and dull bluish green
fix: '(lower leaves) reduced to bladeless sheaths' becomes culm + aphyllopodic FLOPO:0991233. Never read it as 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: The blades are described with a colour.

target: No absence statement for stipule (PO:0020041). The 'more or less persistent' statement probably has another subject in the source (the parse attached it to stipule), so check it before keeping it
fix: 'stipules not seen', 'not observed' and 'unknown' report missing material. They are never an absence, so drop them.
reason: 'Not seen' is a gap in the specimens, not a fact about the plant. A stipule that was not seen cannot also be described as persistent.

target: 'stout' belongs to the peduncle or scape (peduncle PO:0009053), with increased thickness. 'Stemless' means the plant has a very short vegetative stem (stem PO:0009047, decreased length). It does not mean the stem is absent
fix: 'stemless', 'acaulescent' and 'subacaulescent' describe a very short vegetative stem, not an absence. A stout or long axis described in the same taxon is the scape or peduncle (PO:0009053), never 'stem'. Do not map 'scape' to stem when the taxon is called stemless.
reason: Stemless bromeliads still have a stout flowering stalk, and that stalk is what 'stout' describes.

target: No absence statement for fruit (PO:0009001), because the capsules were not seen. 'cylindrical' most likely belongs to another part (for example the perianth tube or the ovary) and should be moved there
fix: 'capsules not seen', 'fruits not seen' and 'fruit unknown' report missing material. They are never an absence, and no fruit statement may come from the same description.
reason: The fruit was not seen, so the cylindrical statement cannot be about the fruit either.

target: Leaf lamina (PO:0020039) absent only on the leaves in the basal 1/3 to 1/2 of the leafy shoot (shoot system PO:0009006), with that range as the context. The blades higher up are present, with the base rounded to obtuse
fix: In Zingiberaceae, '(leafy shoot) bladeless in basal 1/3' and 'bladeless in lower part' give a position on the shoot. Keep the position as the context and never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: The lower sheaths of the leafy shoot have no blade, and the blades above them are described.

target: Leaf (PO:0025034) absent only on the flowering stalk and branches up to near the peduncles, with context 'flowering stalk' or 'peduncle' (PO:0009053). The leaves elsewhere are present and decussate
fix: 'leafless like the branches nearly up to the peduncles' and 'leafless below the inflorescence' give a stretch of the axis. Keep that stretch as the context and never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: Cotyledon has decussate leaves lower down and a bare flowering axis.

target: Glume awn (PO:0025351) absent: the glumes are muticous. The lemma awn (PO:0006032) is present, which is the 'awned' statement
fix: In grasses, 'muticous' and 'awnless' belong to the organ named in the same clause (glume, lemma or palea). Map them to that organ's awn (glume awn PO:0025351, lemma awn PO:0006032, palea awn PO:0025350). Never map them to the generic awn when another organ is described as awned.
reason: Alopecurus has glumes without awns and an awned lemma.

target: Palea (PO:0009038) absent or vestigial only in the sterile or reduced florets, with context 'sterile floret'. The fertile florets have a coriaceous palea
fix: In GrassBase text, 'without significant palea' is said of sterile, apical or reduced florets. Keep the floret type as the context and never record a taxon-wide 'palea absent'.
reason: Elymus fertile florets have a palea. The phrase comes from the description of the reduced florets.

target: The lateral veins (vascular bundle PO:0005020, context 'lateral') of the lower glume (PO:0006002) are absent. The lower glume is present and oblong
fix: '<organ> lateral veins absent' and '<organ> veins absent' map to vascular bundle PO:0005020 absent, with 'lateral' as the context and the organ as the place. The absence never falls on the glume or lemma itself.
reason: The lower glume is described as oblong. Only its side veins are missing.

target: Keel (PO:0025327) absent on the lemma (PO:0009037). The lemma is present and elliptic
fix: 'without keel', 'keel absent' and 'not keeled' map to keel PO:0025327 absent, or to not keeled, on the organ named in the clause. They never map to that organ being absent.
reason: The lemma is described as elliptic. Only its keel is missing.

target: Trichome (PO:0000282) absent on the leaf. The other statement is leaf abaxial stomatal complex (PO:0025190) present, not 'leaf present'
fix: In key-value anatomy text ('Hairs: absent', 'Stomata: present on abaxial surface'), the key names the part. Map the value to that part, with the leaf only as the place. Never map it to the leaf.
reason: Both statements are about cell-level features of the leaf. The hairs are absent and the stomata are present.

target: Pistillate flower (PO:0025599) with context 'allomorphic' absent: these are the odd-shaped female flowers that some Acalypha species have at the tip of the inflorescence. Ordinary flowers are present, and the inflorescence (PO:0009049) is axillary
fix: 'allomorphic pistillate flowers absent' and '<qualifier> <sex> flowers absent' deny only that kind of flower. Map them to the sexed flower class (pistillate flower PO:0025599 or staminate flower PO:0025600), with the qualifier as context. Never map them to a taxon-wide 'flower absent'.
reason: Acalypha virginica has normal male and female flowers. Only the special allomorphic female flowers are missing.
